newsitem.title: CANADA: Teleglobe gets U.S. transmission licence.
newsitem.headline: Teleglobe gets U.S. transmission licence.

text.p: Teleglobe Inc said on Tuesday its U.S. unit Teleglobe USA Inc received a facilities-based license from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC).

The Section 214 authorization permits Teleglobe USA to own and operate international cable and satellite transmission facilities between the United States and virtually every country worldwide, other than Canada, and to establish direct correspodnent agreements with overseas carriers for the exchange of traffic, the company said.
Additional authority for service to and via Canada is being dealt with in separate applications currently pending before the FCC, Teleglobe said.
The new authorization augments Section 214 authority for international resale services, including to Canada and beyond, that Teleglobe USA received from the FCC in July, the company said.

"With the grant of this FCC authority, Teleglobe USA is fully qualified as a facilities-based U.S. international carrier and we will be able to accelerate and complement the implementation of our global network," said Paulo Guidi, president and chief executive of Teleglobe International Corp, the global carrier subsidiary of Teleglobe Inc, in a statement.

Teleglobe USA's east coast gateway switching centre, located in New York, became operational in July and is carrying a growing volume of traffic for Teleglobe's customers nationwide, the company said.
